answers.answer: In the 3-player game, the tied leaders get no coin and the unique last player pays 1 coin. In an unequal 2-player Census, the unique leader gains 1 coin, while the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Census: tied lead gives no coin; unique last pays 1; in a 2-player game the last player never pays, but a unique leader still gains 1 coin.

answers.answer: You do not have to draw six; you may draw at most two because only two Market spaces are free. Unused Market Followers remain there between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Followers: draw any number up to the Knights Track allowance, limited by free Market spaces; unused Market Followers remain between rounds and occupy capacity.

answers.answer: You may fill an action gradually over multiple rounds, but cannot activate it until all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall needs only one of its two spaces). A full activation may be saved for a later round. When an ordinary action is executed, its Followers return to your bag.
answers.evidence: Planning: fill an action gradually; activated only when all required spaces are occupied; an activation can be saved. Actions: after an ordinary action, return its Followers to your bag.

answers.answer: Starting with the Start Player and proceeding clockwise repeatedly, each player takes one activated action or passes. Passing ends your participation for the Action Phase, so you cannot act again that round. Unused activations keep their Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Actions: take one activated action or pass; passing ends your participation; unused activations keep their Followers on the board for future rounds.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances the Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted at that track space.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Farm House: “Put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.”

answers.answer: Village can recruit a Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader, putting the recruit in your bag and advancing that profession's track one space. Boatman gives the depicted coins, except at the last space the first player there gets a Citizen instead. Craftsman gives a Technology tile, usable only after you pass. Trader gives a Place Tile: first advance allows category I only; later advances allow I or II.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment: put the chosen neutral Follower in your bag and advance its profession track; listed Boatman, Craftsman, and Trader rewards.

answers.answer: No. A newly acquired Craftsman's Technology can only be used after you pass and cannot help execute another action that round after that pass. Your first placed Technology must replace a Farmer. Later Technology may replace any profession except Monk. At most one Technology per Place; none at a Place requiring only one Follower; once placed, it cannot be moved.
answers.evidence: Technology: first placed Technology must replace a Farmer; later ones may replace any profession except Monk; never more than one at a single Place or at a one-Follower Place; cannot be moved. Craftsman tile is used only after passing.

answers.answer: No. The first Traders Track advance permits category I only. Every later advance permits category I or II. Players may inspect the stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Setup: players may inspect Place Tile stacks at any time. Village recruitment, Trader: first advance permits category I only; every later advance allows I or II.

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances the Scholars Track one space, and awards the depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances the Knights Track; the fourth Knight keeps the allowance at 7 and gives its Citizen to the first player there. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. Once a character track is on its last space, you cannot take that corresponding action again.
answers.evidence: Actions table and Castle rewards; Character-track limits: once on a track's last space, you cannot take the corresponding action again.

answers.answer: A Monk may replace a Knight for an ordinary action. A Knight or Technology cannot replace a required Monk. A Monk also cannot replace the exact profession required on a Beneficial Deed.
answers.evidence: Monks: on ordinary actions a Monk can replace any other profession; reverse is forbidden. Town Hall: substitutions, including Monks and Place abilities, cannot replace exact professions depicted on Deeds.

answers.answer: A Ship moves the Merchant one Waterway connection to an adjacent town; a Wagon moves one Road connection to an adjacent town. You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if several lie there. Empty connections are legal and yield no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: one Ship/Wagon traverses one connection; may take one good, choosing if several lie there; empty Roads/Waterways are legal.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the town where your Merchant currently is. A town with any player's station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Building: Guildhall requires your Merchant in the town; a town with any player's Trading Station cannot receive another. Orléans exception allows one per player.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gains 1 Development Point by moving one space on the Development Track. When moving onto or past a coin space, collect its coins; the first player onto or past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; on reaching or passing a Development Status space, Status immediately becomes its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Scriptorium: gain 1 Development Point. Scoring: moving onto or past coin/Citizen spaces gives the stated rewards; reaching/passing a Status space changes Status immediately.

answers.answer: Town Hall works with one or two eligible Followers; you may send either one or both in an action. Your four marked starting Followers cannot be used. Each sent neutral Follower goes permanently to a free Deed space matching its exact profession and earns that space's depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; Canalization offers 1 coin or 1 Development Point. The player filling a Deed's last space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: send one or both; starting Followers may not enter; exact-profession free spaces; rewards; last-space Citizen.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment during Phase 5 (Actions); it takes effect before the Event Phase. Other events resolve in Phase 6. The top Hour Glass tile is Pilgrimage, so it opens the game.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Phase 1 reveals tile; Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5; Phase 6 is Event. Setup: Pilgrimage is put on top, so round 1 always has it.

answers.answer: Only grain, cheese, or wine qualifies as food; wool does not. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you cannot pay food, you owe 5 coins; if you have fewer than five coins, pay what you can and undergo torture for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Harvest: pay one grain, cheese, or wine to Goods Market; if unable, pay 5 coins; unable to pay those coins means torture for shortfall. Wool and brocade are not food. Torture: pay available coins and replace each missing coin with an item.

answers.answer: The neutral Scholar returns to its game-board supply and becomes recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. The colored starting Trader is kept and no Follower is lost that round; you do not redraw.
answers.evidence: Plague: neutral Follower returns to game-board supply; do not move its track marker back. If a marked starting Follower is drawn, keep it and lose no Follower; do not redraw.

answers.answer: Pay the one coin you have, then cover each of the two missing coins with one item per coin. Choices include a built or unbuilt Trading Station; a random eligible neutral Follower drawn from your bag (return and redraw marked starting Followers); one Development Point moving left but never onto or past a coin space; one Goods Tile, Place Tile, or Technology tile. Starting Followers cannot be surrendered. Surrendered items are removed from the game.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy): pay available coins and replace each missing coin with an item from the listed mix; marked starting Followers always stay; surrendered items are removed from the game.

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if the action would otherwise give another reward. It becomes available again when the required tile is available, subject to normal requirements. If the common coin supply is insufficient, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies: cannot play an action providing an unavailable tile, including if another part gives a reward; available again when stock returns; insufficient coin supply means no coins received then.

answers.answer: A tie for most built stations gives the bonus Citizen to nobody. Each grain scores 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, and brocade 5 points. Stations and collected Citizens score (number of built stations + number of Citizens) × final Development Status. Tied final scores go to the player furthest ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, victory is shared.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: unique most stations takes set-aside Citizen; tie gives nobody. Possession table lists goods values and station/Citizen formula; tie-break rule follows.

answers.answer: Each player receives a board, bag, Merchant, 10 Trading Stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers (Farmer, Boatman, Craftsman, Trader). Place starting Followers on the Market, Merchant in Orléans, and one marker on the first space of each of six Character Tracks and the Development Track. Keep coins and unbuilt stations in front of you. The youngest player starts.
answers.evidence: Setup, player equipment and placements; final setup sentence: youngest player takes the Start Player token.

answers.answer: Put 13 Citizens on their marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final Trading Station award. Sort neutral Followers by profession into their game-board buildings and Technology into its supply. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II. In four players, shuffle goods face down and deal one face up to every eligible Road/Waterway goods space; sort remaining goods face up into the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 3, and 5; fewer-player note states in 4-player games fill every such space.

answers.answer: In 3 players remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders each; 3 neutral Knights, Scholars, and Monks each; remove 6 random goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. In 2 players remove 4 of each of the first group; 6 of each of the second group; remove 12 random goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Fewer players table and first sentence: remove all starting Followers of unused colors.

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
answers.evidence: Actions table, required professions column.

answers.answer: Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
answers.evidence: Actions table, required professions column.

answers.answer: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall permits 1 or 2 eligible Followers; during Planning, place one or two neutral Followers there, and marked starting Followers are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Actions table lists Scriptorium and Town Hall costs; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds specifies neutral Followers and starting-Follower exclusion.

answers.answer: Yes. For each draw declined, you may move one Follower from an Action Space back to your Market, so declining two draws can recover two Followers. You cannot move a Follower directly from one Action Space to another.
answers.evidence: Followers phase: for each draw declined, may move one Follower from an Action Space back to Market; this is the permitted recovery method, not direct transfer between Action Spaces.

answers.answer: Yes. You may inspect your bag at any time, but must shuffle its contents afterward.
answers.evidence: Followers phase: “You may inspect your bag at any time, but shuffle its contents afterward.”

answers.answer: The phases are Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, Actions, Event, Start Player. The Start Player token passes to the player on your left. Planning begins simultaneously; announce completion, and if order matters, plan clockwise from Start Player. Payments and order-sensitive Event resolution proceed clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to the common supply; received coins come from it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure lists seven phases and specifies clockwise ordering in Planning and Event; coins paid go to common supply and received coins come from it; Start Player passes left.

answers.answer: You finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including that round's event; scoring is after that.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: “Finish the entire round in which the 18th Hour Glass tile is drawn, including its event.”

answers.answer: The uniquely leading player on the Farmers Track gains the Census coin, regardless of the number of Farmer tiles in anyone's bag.
answers.evidence: Census: compare markers on Farmers Track, regardless of Farmer tiles currently in bags; unique leader gains 1 coin.

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to your current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Events table, Income: gain coins equal to Development Status.

answers.answer: Eight goods count as two complete groups of three, so you pay 2 coins. The calculation counts all goods, regardless of type. If you cannot make the payment, undergo torture for the shortfall.
answers.evidence: Taxes: count all goods and pay 1 coin per complete group of 3 (round down); a shortfall causes torture.

answers.answer: You receive 4 coins, based on the four built Trading Stations; unbuilt reserve stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Trading Day: gain 1 coin per built Trading Station. Building section: only built stations count for income.

answers.answer: Hayrick costs Farmer and takes 1 grain from the Goods Market; Cheese Factory costs Farmer + Farmer and takes 1 cheese from the Goods Market; Winery costs Farmer + Trader and takes 1 wine from the Goods Market; Wool Manufacturer costs Boatman + Trader and takes 1 wool from the Goods Market; Tailor Shop costs Scholar + Trader and takes 1 brocade from the Goods Market. A goods-producing Place cannot be used when its particular good is absent from the Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles table lists the five costs and goods-market effects; following sentence bars use when the particular good is absent.

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman, gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk, gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman, gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar, gain 2 Development Points.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles table, entries for Shipping Line, Brewery, Windmill, and Library.

answers.answer: Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins, advancing one Development space per coin; paying two advances two spaces. Zero or four coins is not allowed.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles, Pharmacy: any 1 Follower; pay 1–3 coins; advance one space per coin; must spend at least 1 and no more than 3.

answers.answer: Cellar: Monk + Scholar, gain 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar, gain 1 coin per built Trading Station. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar, gain coins equal to current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles table lists costs/effects; Office uses number of built stations, Hospital uses current Development Status.

answers.answer: Horse Wagon is activated by Trader + Knight. It moves along one Road connection to an adjacent town and collects one good if available.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles, Horse Wagon: Trader + Knight; move along one Road to adjacent town and collect one good if available.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile, subject to normal placement constraints. Your first Technology cannot be placed on Laboratory because it has no Farmer space; a later Technology may go on either Laboratory space if none is already there and normal constraints are met.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles, Laboratory entry and its bold clarification about first and later Technology placement.

answers.answer: Bathhouse costs one Farmer. Draw three Followers from your bag, choose two, and immediately place the chosen Followers on appropriate Action Spaces; none may go on Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and the activating Bathhouse Farmer to your bag.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles, Bathhouse: Farmer; draw 3, choose 2, immediately place; none on Bathhouse; return third and activating tile.

answers.answer: You may place the one Follower that can legally go on an allowed Action Space. Return the other two drawn Followers and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: Bathhouse: if you can legally place only one or none, do so and return all other drawn Followers to bag; return activating Follower too.

answers.answer: It may be executed later in the same Action Phase if you have not passed. The summary says newly acquired Places and their abilities are available immediately during the current Action Phase, and players may choose action order freely; passing ends participation.
answers.evidence: Trader recruitment: acquired Place and passive ability available immediately, including current Action Phase. Planning: activation can be saved; Actions: choose action order freely and passing ends participation.

answers.answer: Sacristy costs a Monk. If activated, during Phase 6 it protects against a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague; return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering the event.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles, Sacristy entry: Monk; protects against negative event; during Phase 6 return Monk to bag instead of suffering event.

answers.answer: No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5 Actions; Sacristy's protection is used later in Phase 6, so activating Sacristy does not override that restriction.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5. Sacristy protection is applied during Phase 6.

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not allow replacement of Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles, Herb Garden: Boatmen may replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions.

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It requires no activation. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles: School has no activation and Scholars may replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions.

answers.answer: No. Beneficial Deeds require the exact professions depicted, and Place substitutions cannot replace those professions. Using Gunpowder Tower instead of Town Hall does not change this; its Deed spaces still require exact types.
answers.evidence: Town Hall: substitutions, including Place abilities, cannot replace exact Deed professions. Gunpowder Tower: Deed spaces still require exact types.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3, place 1 or 2 drawn Followers there. During Planning move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, during Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in a single action. Marked starting Followers cannot be sent; Deed spaces still require exact types.
answers.evidence: Base Place Tiles, Gunpowder Tower entry.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin. The two players tied furthest behind pay nothing because a tied last place pays nothing.
answers.evidence: Census: unique leader gains 1 coin; tied last place pays nothing.

answers.answer: The uniquely leading player takes the set-aside Citizen before scoring, after the game ends. It counts as a collected Citizen in final scoring, included with built stations in the formula multiplied by final Development Status.
answers.evidence: Scoring: before scoring, unique most built stations takes set-aside Citizen. Final formula counts built stations plus collected Citizens.

answers.answer: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, then put Pilgrimage on top. In Phase 1, the Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup: Hour Glass stack preparation; Turn Structure, Phase 1: Start Player reveals the top tile.

answers.answer: Each remaining coin is worth 1 victory point.
answers.evidence: Scoring table: Coins — 1 each.

answers.answer: Initial Development Status is 1 and initial Knight-track draw allowance is 4.
answers.evidence: Setup step 2: Development Status starts at 1; initial draw allowance is 4.

answers.answer: Only lost Development Points can be regained. Surrendered goods, Followers, stations, Places, and Technology are removed from the game rather than returned to supplies.
answers.evidence: Torture: items surrendered are removed from game; only lost Development Points can be regained.

answers.answer: You may choose the order freely; you are not bound by printed board order or order of filling.
answers.evidence: Actions phase: “Choose your actions' order freely.”

answers.answer: Its passive substitution ability is available as soon as you acquire the Place, including during the current Action Phase.
answers.evidence: Trader recruitment: acquired Place and its passive special ability are available immediately, including during current Action Phase.

answers.answer: You may send just one; Town Hall allows sending one or both eligible Followers in an action.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds: in one Town Hall action, send one or both.

answers.answer: You may leave the good there. The rule says you may take one good from the connection, so taking it is optional.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: “You may take one good from that connection,” choosing one if several lie there.

answers.answer: Yes. You may send the second on a later action turn in the same Action Phase before passing; the two transfers need not occur in one action.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Town Hall's two Followers may be sent in separate action turns during the same Action Phase, before passing.
